label: Greater Angkor archaeological lower bound with declared endpoint precision
lower_bound_tolerance_evidence: The published 700,000 endpoint is an approximate archaeological reconstruction whose range is driven by uncertain embankment occupation. A predeclared 0.5 percent numerical endpoint tolerance is used only for one-sided scoring; it is not a population uncertainty interval and cannot set global scale.
pressure_evidence: Klassen et al. 2021, Science Advances 7, eabf8441, abstract and Table 1: approximately 700,000-900,000 people in the fixed 3,000 km2 Greater Angkor Region at the 12th-13th-century apogee.
Klassen et al. 2021, pp. 4-5: agricultural metropolitan growth slowed to zero in AD 1181-1300 and farming communities occupied the hydraulic landscape.
Klassen et al. 2022, Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory 29, pp. 763-794: more than 1,000 km2 of Angkor-period rice fields and organized local agricultural provisioning.
boundary_description: Approximately 3,000 km2 Greater Angkor Region watershed catchment including agricultural communities, hydraulic infrastructure and the civic-ceremonial center; not a city-only label.
boundary_source: Klassen et al. 2021, Figure 1 and pp. 1, 5.
notes: Retained as a low-confidence one-sided validation/floor. The tolerance is a declared generic evidence-precision contract, not an Angkor-specific model correction.
